Teaching AI to say yes is easy. Teaching it when to say ‘no,’ ‘I don’t know,’ or ‘let me get a human’ is the actual job. Our client is hiring an Applied AI Engineer to build the second kind.
The Applied AI Engineer designs, builds and tests the AI conversations and agents inside the client’s learner-facing products: advisory experiences, practice simulations and diagnostic coaching.
They work with Product, Content Studios, Engineering and subject-matter experts. They turn product and instructional requirements into reliable AI behavior, prove it through testing, and keep it performing after release.
This company is at the forefront of learning technologies, providing e-learning programs for professionals in regulated industries such as healthcare and finance. They’re constantly evolving and growing, run efficient Agile-first teams, and have a broadly distributed staff. They value good-natured, inquisitive, and methodical IT professionals who come prepared to collaborate and share their knowledge.
Your responsibilities will include:
Turn scenario specs, decision models and assessment rubrics into prompts, application logic and testable behavior.
Spot missing requirements and technical constraints, and raise them with Product, Engineering and SMEs.
Define how AI models connect to application services and approved data sources: APIs, tool interactions, data structures, validation, error handling, permitted actions.
Design prompts, structured outputs and validation logic, and catch invalid responses before they reach learners.
Build conversational runtimes with controlled personas, session state and explicit state transitions.
Keep simulation behavior, assessment logic and feedback separate, so feedback cannot change assessment results.
Implement grounding and retrieval from approved knowledge sources, with source references where required.
Keep code, prompts, schemas and evaluation assets under version control, and document them.
Run bounded experiments with Product, with clear questions and success measures.
Take validated prototypes into production with Engineering, and check behavior stays the same.
Help build the technical controls that keep AI features compliant with accreditation requirements (issue flagging, review steps, disclosure, logging).
What are the required skills?
Expert prompt and context engineering: system prompts, few-shot examples, prompt chaining, routing, breaking complex tasks into steps
Structured outputs with JSON Schema, function calling and validation layers, with retry and fallback logic
RAG design: chunking, metadata filtering, hybrid search, reranking, citation grounding
Managing token budgets, prompt caching, context compaction and long-session memory
Agentic systems: tool use, planner/executor patterns, multi-agent orchestration, state machines, human-in-the-loop checkpoints
Defining tool schemas, permission scopes and action limits for agents
AI evaluation: golden datasets, rubric-based scoring, LLM-as-judge calibrated against human raters, regression testing
LLM observability and tracing
LLM security: prompt injection, data leakage, jailbreaks, unsafe tool actions, and guardrails
Comparing prompting, retrieval and model options on quality, latency and cost
Python or TypeScript, including API integrations and automated testing
Git (e.g. Bitbucket), reproducible tests and CI
Works with AI coding agents by default
Explains technical trade-offs to non-technical colleagues
Sound judgment on privacy, human oversight and the limits of AI-generated assessment or advice
Hands-on experience building LLM applications with multi-step conversational workflows
Experience collaborating with subject-matter experts
Preferred
Background in learning products, assessment, simulations or regulated professional content

**Our Operating Principles**
***Extreme Ownership***
We take full responsibility for our work, outcomes, and team success. No excuses, no blame-shifting — if something needs fixing, we own it and make it better. This means stepping up, even when it’s not “your job.” If a ball is dropped, we pick it up. If a customer is unhappy, we fix it. If a process is broken, we redesign it. We don’t wait for someone else to solve it — we lead with accountability and expect the same from those around us.
  
  
***Craftsmanship***
Putting care and intention into every task, striving for excellence, and taking deep ownership of the quality and outcome of your work. Craftsmanship means never settling for “just fine.” We sweat the details because details compound. Whether it’s a product feature, an internal doc, or a sales call — we treat it as a reflection of our standards. We aim to deliver jaw-dropping customer experiences by being curious, meticulous, and proud of what we build — even when nobody’s watching.
  
  
***We are “majos”***
Be friendly & have fun with your coworkers. Always be genuine & honest, but kind. “Majo” is our way of saying: be a good human. Be approachable, helpful, and warm. We’re building something ambitious, and it’s easier (and more fun) when we enjoy the ride together. We give feedback with kindness, challenge each other with respect, and celebrate wins together without ego.
  
  
***Urgency with Focus***
Create the highest impact in the shortest amount of time. Move fast, but in the right direction. We operate with speed because time is our most limited resource. But speed without focus is chaos. We prioritize ruthlessly, act decisively, and stay aligned. We aim for high leverage: the biggest results from the simplest, smartest actions. We’re running a high-speed marathon — not a sprint with no strategy.
  
  
***Talent Density and Meritocracy***
Hire only people who can raise the average; ‘exceptional performance is the passing grade.’ Ability trumps seniority. We believe the best teams are built on talent density — every hire should raise the bar. We reward contribution, not titles or tenure. We give ownership to those who earn it, and we all hold each other to a high standard. A-players want to work with other A-players — that’s how we win.
  
  
***First-Principles Thinking***
Strip a problem to physics-level facts, ignore industry dogma, rebuild the solution from scratch. We don’t copy-paste solutions. We go back to basics, ask why things are the way they are, and rebuild from the ground up if needed. This mindset pushes us to innovate, challenge stale assumptions, and move faster than incumbents. It’s how we build what others think is impossible.
